- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) and forecast spikes sharply, cap or dampen the overshoot to avoid overreacting to sentiment-driven volatility.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) and forecast is high, reduce the forecast by 10–20% to reflect bearish sentiment bias.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days trending down), apply a downward bias correction.  
- If forecast shows extreme outliers (e.g., > 3x median or < 1/3 median), flag for sentiment alignment — if sentiment is neutral or negative, suppress extreme highs or lows.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/– 0.33), avoid overfitting to short-term sentiment swings; use 3–5 day smoothing or lagged sentiment as a filter.  
- For forecasts with high variance or erratic spikes, apply a “sentiment-weighted smoothing” rule: if sentiment is stable, use 3-day moving average; if sentiment is volatile, use 7-day average.
